subtitle: Leadership Succession — Bench Strength Assessment, High-Potential Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps

document_brief.narrative_theme: This succession plan establishes enterprise readiness for leadership continuity by quantifying bench strength for critical roles, naming high-potential successors, detailing time-bound development actions, and highlighting emergency coverage gaps requiring immediate mitigation.

sections.heading: Enterprise Bench Strength Assessment for Critical Leadership Roles (FY2026)
key_facts: As of 2026-05-01, the succession slate covers 12 critical roles across the enterprise.
Bench strength is rated Ready Now for 4 of 12 roles, Ready in 1–2 Years for 5 of 12 roles, and No Identified Successor for 3 of 12 roles.
The three roles with No Identified Successor are Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Head of Supply Chain, and VP, Customer Support.

sections.heading: High-Potential Successor Identification, Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps

By 2026-09-30, each high-potential candidate will complete 2 development actions: one cross-functional rotation and one executive sponsor assignment.

structure.heading: Enterprise Bench Strength Assessment for Critical Leadership Roles (FY2026)
text_content: **Enterprise Bench Strength Assessment for Critical Leadership Roels (FY2026)**

As of 20260-5-01, the succession slate covers 12 critical roles across the enterprise. Bench strength is rated Ready Now for 4 of 12 roles, Ready in 1–2 Years for 5 of 12 roles, and No Identified Successor for 3 of 12 roles. This distribution equates to 33.3% Ready Now, 41.7% Ready in 1 to 2 years, and 25.0% with no identified successor, highlighting a concentrated shortfall. The current inventory was validated against organizational charts, performance data, and role criitcality metrics.

The distribution signals elevated enterprise risk that requires immediate governance attention from the Board of Directors, the CEO, and the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO). With 33.3% of critical roles Ready Now, we lack immediate depth for 66.7% of positions, creating potential continuity exposure in high-volume business units and regulatory functions. Talent investments should rpioritize accelerated leadership programs, cross-functional rotations, and a 12–24 month internal mobility target to shift two Ready in 1–2 Years successors into Ready Now status by Q2 FY2027.

The three roles with No Identified Successor are Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Head of Supply Chain, and VP, Customer Support. Immediate actions include designation of interim owners within 30 days, initiation of focused external candidate searches with executive search partners by 2026-06-01, and fast-track development plans for internal candidates to be assessed quarterly. An emergency succession playbook will be published by the CHRO by 2026-06-15 and include 90-day stabilization protocols, role-specific KPIs, contingency reporting lines, and monitoring cadence.

structure.heading: High-Potential Successor Identification, Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps
text_content: **High-Potential Successor Identification, Development Plans, and Emergency Succession Gaps**

The high-potential successor pool includes nine named candidates: Aisha Khan, Miguel Santos, Priya Patel, Jordan Lee, Chen Wei, Sofia Rossi, Daniel Okafor, Emma Johnson, and Ravi Menon. These individuals were identified through calibrated performance ratings, leadership assessments, and strategic role-alignment reviews. This cohort represents 75% of targeted mid-to-senior talent identified in the enterprise assessment and will be tracked against competency milestones and retention indicators.

Each high-potential candidate will complete two development actions by 2026-09-30: one cross-functional rotation and one executive sponsor assignment. Development plans will be individualized, measurable, and reviewed quarterly by the Talent Council. Priority activities include 1) 6–12 month rotational placements, 2) executive sponsorship with defined goals, and 3) targeted leadership training. Progress metrics will inform promotion readiness and succession readiness scoring and retention risk mitigation.

Emergency succession coverage is defined as a designated interim leader available within 72 hours. As of 2026-05-01, three of twelve critical roles do not meet this standard. To remediate, assign named contingency interims, document handover protocols, and provide accelerated readiness coaching over a 60-day window. Completion of gap closures will be monitored monthly; unresolved exposures will escalate to the Executive Risk Committee for review.
